claims.claim: C1: Age-dependent posterior re-weighting of provisionally-clean commits (LAW) improves online JIT-SDP over waiting-time baselines
closest_prior: Liu et al. 2024a PU learning for JIT-SDP, Empir Softw Eng 29(5):98 — NOT YET OPENED
claims.exact_difference: ODaSC derives label confidence from feature-space micro-clusters for examples already labelled clean after W days; LAW derives it from commit age via a right-truncation-corrected discovery-delay distribution combined with model risk, and also trains on commits younger than W. Difference vs CVR methods: domain transfer + truncation-aware nonparametric delay estimate (weaker).
claims.status: FAILING ON DEV (cycle 1): LAW loses to tuned wait/ORB on dev projects; see journal FAILURE/DIAGNOSIS. Liu 2024a UNVERIFIED.

claims.claim: C2 (Type A/C): waiting time barely denoises labels; its effect is mainly class-composition shift of recent data
claims.status: model-free evidence on 14 projects; needs a model-based confirmation (E3 diag)

claims.claim: C3 (Type C): most of the verification-latency penalty in online JIT-SDP is due to training-set composition (missing young commits), not label noise
closest_prior: Cabral ICSE 2019 / Cabral & Minku TSE 2022 (waiting-time trade-off)
Song, Minku & Yao EMSE 2023 (evaluation validity vs W)
claims.exact_difference: Prior work treats the penalty as label noise vs staleness; we measure it with a true-label decomposition (denoise-only vs add-young-bugs vs oracle) on 14 projects

claims.claim: C4 (Type E): adaptive per-project waiting time from the online truncation-corrected delay estimate removes the need to tune W
closest_prior: Cabral ICSE 2019 (single W=90 chosen from delay analysis)
claims.exact_difference: W is re-estimated per project at each update from the Lagakos survival curve instead of fixed globally
claims.status: E0b dev; prior-art queries 1/8 done (web: 'adaptive waiting time verification latency JIT-SDP' — no match)

claims.claim: C5 (Type B): dormant-bug posterior from mature-only, cross-fitted scorers x truncation-corrected delay survival, applied to the wait set, beats tuned waiting/ORB/ODaSC-style in online JIT-SDP
closest_prior: Falessi et al. TOSEM 2021 dormant defects
claims.exact_difference: Unlike DEFUSE/ES-DFM the fake-negative probability is not learned by the online model (which we show self-confirms in JIT-SDP: LAW-model) but by scorers trained only on mature commits and cross-fitted, combined with a right-truncation-corrected delay survival; unlike ODaSC the confidence uses commit age and a supervised scorer instead of micro-cluster class composition.

claims.claim: C3: Under verification latency, label-policy differences in online JIT-SDP are mainly operating-point effects; a latency-aware decision threshold (LAT: G-mean-optimal threshold on recent prequential scores with delay-survival-weighted provisional labels) beats fixed waiting times and generic mature-label threshold moving (MAT)
closest_prior: ORB (Cabral et al. 2019): adjusts class weights from the predicted-positive moving average
claims.exact_difference: LAT sets the decision threshold from recent scored commits whose provisional labels are weighted by a right-truncation-corrected discovery-delay survival, so it can use commits younger than any waiting time; ORB changes training weights toward a fixed target positive rate, GHOST/MAT use only labelled/mature data, ODaSC changes sampling not the threshold.
claims.status: archived with magical-bardeen plan_v2 (not carried forward: threshold effects small for denoisers, diag_threshold_dev.json)

scores.claim: C3 noise-dominance (H3) + negative result for age-based correction (LAW/awt)
scores.notes: Dormant-defects TOSEM 2021 and ODaSC frame the same noise; our decomposition quantifies it for online JIT-SDP (strong stats, 10/10 projects) but there is no working method yet. Blind review not run.
